title: Interpretable Network-assisted Random Forest+
abstract: arXiv:2509.15611v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Machine learning algorithms often assume that training samples are independent. When data points are connected by a network, the induced dependency between samples is both a challenge, reducing effective sample size, and an opportunity to improve prediction by leveraging information from network neighbors. Multiple methods taking advantage of this opportunity are available, but many, including graph neural networks, are not easily interpretable, limiting their usefulness for understanding how models make predictions. Others, such as network-assisted linear regression, are interpretable but often yield worse prediction performance. translated_title: 可解释的网络辅助随机森林+
translated_abstract: 机器学习算法通常假设训练样本是相互独立的。当数据点通过网络相互连接时，样本之间产生的依赖性既是挑战（降低了有效样本量），也是机遇（可以利用网络邻居的信息来改进预测）。目前已有多种利用这一机遇的方法，但其中许多方法（包括图神经网络）不易解释，限制了其在理解模型如何进行预测方面的实用性。其他方法，如网络辅助线性回归，虽然具有可解释性，但预测性能往往较差。我们通过提出一族基于随机森林泛化（RF+）构建的灵活的网络辅助模型来弥合这一差距，该模型实现了极具竞争力的预测精度，并且可以通过直接从模型参数和结构推导出的内在可解释性度量来加以理解。
tldr: 本文提出了一种基于随机森林泛化（RF+）的可解释网络辅助模型族，在实现极具竞争力的预测精度的同时，通过直接从模型参数和结构推导出的内在可解释性度量，弥合了网络辅助预测中预测性能与可解释性之间的差距。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a family of interpretable network-assisted models built upon a generalization of random forests (RF+), which achieves highly-competitive prediction accuracy while bridging the gap between performance and interpretability through intrinsic interpretability measures derived directly from the model parameters and structure.
